newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai military to scale down spending on equipment.
newsitem.headline: Thai military to scale down spending on equipment.

text.p: Defence Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Thursday that the Thai military would scale down spending, which would affect plans to buy a $1.2 billion spy satellite system and other hardware.

Chavalit, who initiated the spy sattelite project and agreed to modernise the miitary with advanced and high technology, told Reuters in an interview the cut in spending was because of a national economic downturn.
His plan to buy the spy satellite system had been criticised by some politicians who felt that such a large amount of money was not worth spending on a single project.
"From now on, any project that costs a lot money, we will have to slow down. This is due to the economic slowdown and problems with the current account deficit " he said.
Thailand's current account deficit this year is at a worrisome level and is expected to widen. It stood at a high 8.1 percent of gross domestic product in 1995.
Chavalit said if the military really needed to buy weapons and other necessities that are expensive, it would have to do so on countertrade basis.
The military had proposed a long shopping list during the 14-month administration of outgoing premier Banharn Silpa-archa.
Included in the list were plans to buy 228 armoured cars worth $280 million from a French company and a $578 million pact to buy a squadron of F/A-18 "Hornet" jet fighters from the United States.
